pass_standard: Pass when the assessment uses the closed impact taxonomy, stays within the exact claim and thesis mechanism, and explains its conclusion without a material unsupported inference.
An insufficient assessment passes when it names the missing decision-useful evidence and asks a follow-up capable of closing that gap.
A passing verifier output has no findings.
reject_standard: Reject exact binding or driver drift, a material unsupported inference, a wrong closed-taxonomy impact, an internally contradictory rationale, or an insufficient follow-up that cannot close the stated gap.
Do not invent binding or driver mismatches when the quoted values match, and do not propose impact synonyms outside supports, weakens, no_change, or insufficient.
A rejecting verifier output has at least one closed finding whose severity is fixed by its code.

cases.title: Gate 2 revenue growth is correctly insufficient for operating leverage

claim.normalized_statement: Microsoft quarterly revenue increased 18.3% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Quarterly revenue growth sustains operating leverage.

assessment.driver_statement: Quarterly revenue growth sustains operating leverage.
assessment.rationale: Revenue growth confirms the revenue-side precondition but operating income, margin, and cost growth are missing, so operating leverage cannot yet be determined.
assessment.follow_up_question: Did operating income or operating margin rise year over year, and did operating expenses grow more slowly than revenue?

gold.rationale: The assessment does not claim operating leverage occurred; it identifies the exact evidence gap and asks a follow-up that can close it.

findings.detail: The refs and hashes match the quoted objects, but the thesis id lacks a prefix and was incorrectly treated as a mismatch.
The driver matches the thesis mechanism exactly, but the matching value was incorrectly reported as a mismatch.
The verifier treated identification of the revenue-side precondition as a claim that operating leverage occurred.
The verifier proposed none or contradictory, which are outside the closed impact taxonomy.
The verifier said the assessment hash could not be checked even though the canonical assessment and content hash were supplied.

cases.title: Exact customer growth supports the demand mechanism

claim.normalized_statement: Paying enterprise customers increased 31% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Enterprise customer adoption drives durable subscription demand.

assessment.driver_statement: Enterprise customer adoption drives durable subscription demand.
assessment.rationale: The exact customer-growth claim is directly consistent with the adoption mechanism.

gold.rationale: The claim directly measures the bound mechanism and the assessment stays directional.

cases.title: Customer contraction weakens the adoption mechanism

claim.normalized_statement: Paying enterprise customers declined 9% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Enterprise customer adoption drives durable subscription demand.

assessment.driver_statement: Enterprise customer adoption drives durable subscription demand.
assessment.rationale: The reported contraction is directionally inconsistent with the adoption mechanism.

gold.rationale: The assessment uses a direct, bounded directional inference.

cases.title: Unrelated tax-rate movement leaves the demand mechanism unchanged

claim.normalized_statement: The quarterly effective tax rate increased by 120 basis points.

thesis.mechanism: Enterprise customer adoption drives durable subscription demand.

assessment.driver_statement: Enterprise customer adoption drives durable subscription demand.
assessment.rationale: The tax-rate claim does not bear on enterprise customer adoption or subscription demand.

gold.rationale: The assessment correctly distinguishes unrelated evidence from missing evidence about the mechanism.

cases.title: A precise follow-up makes an evidence-gap assessment valid

claim.normalized_statement: Gross billings increased 22% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Higher billings convert into durable free cash flow.

assessment.driver_statement: Higher billings convert into durable free cash flow.
assessment.rationale: Billings growth is established, but cash collections, working capital, and capital expenditure are absent.
assessment.follow_up_question: Did operating cash flow grow and free-cash-flow margin expand in the same period after working-capital and capital-expenditure effects?

gold.rationale: The assessment identifies the conversion gap and asks for the exact cash-flow evidence needed.

cases.title: Claim hash is bound to the wrong formal claim

claim.normalized_statement: Revenue increased 14% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Revenue growth sustains operating leverage.

assessment.driver_statement: Revenue growth sustains operating leverage.
assessment.rationale: Revenue growth is consistent with the mechanism.

gold.rationale: The assessment claim hash differs from the exact quoted ClaimVersion hash.

cases.title: Driver statement is not the exact thesis mechanism

claim.normalized_statement: Revenue increased 14% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Revenue growth sustains operating leverage.

assessment.driver_statement: Revenue growth guarantees higher earnings per share.
assessment.rationale: Revenue growth is consistent with the substituted driver.

gold.rationale: The assessment replaced the exact operating-leverage mechanism with an EPS guarantee.

cases.title: Revenue growth alone is overclaimed as margin expansion

claim.normalized_statement: Revenue increased 5% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Operating-margin expansion demonstrates scalable unit economics.

assessment.driver_statement: Operating-margin expansion demonstrates scalable unit economics.
assessment.rationale: Revenue growth proves operating margin expanded and unit economics scaled.

gold.rationale: The exact claim contains no operating-margin or cost evidence.

cases.title: A demand contraction is assigned the wrong directional impact

claim.normalized_statement: Active customers declined 12% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Customer adoption expands recurring demand.

assessment.driver_statement: Customer adoption expands recurring demand.
assessment.rationale: The customer decline supports the adoption mechanism.

gold.rationale: The claim direction weakens rather than supports the mechanism.

cases.title: Rationale contradicts a supports label

claim.normalized_statement: Net retention increased from 104% to 112%.

thesis.mechanism: Expansion within existing accounts sustains recurring growth.

assessment.driver_statement: Expansion within existing accounts sustains recurring growth.
assessment.rationale: Net retention is unrelated to expansion within existing accounts and provides no evidence for the mechanism.

gold.rationale: The rationale denies relevance while the impact says supports.

cases.title: Vague follow-up cannot close the stated cash-flow gap

claim.normalized_statement: Bookings increased 18% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Bookings convert into free cash flow without working-capital strain.

assessment.driver_statement: Bookings convert into free cash flow without working-capital strain.
assessment.rationale: Bookings are known, but conversion, working capital, and cash flow are missing.

gold.rationale: The follow-up does not identify cash conversion, working capital, or free cash flow.

cases.title: Constant-currency growth is mislabeled as weakening demand

claim.normalized_statement: Reported revenue declined 2%, while constant-currency revenue increased 7%.

thesis.mechanism: Underlying customer demand produces organic revenue growth.

assessment.driver_statement: Underlying customer demand produces organic revenue growth.
assessment.rationale: The reported-currency decline shows underlying customer demand contracted.

gold.rationale: The exact claim reports positive constant-currency growth, so reported FX translation does not weaken underlying demand.

cases.title: Stable gross retention supports the recurring-revenue mechanism

claim.normalized_statement: Subscription gross retention remained at 96% for the third consecutive quarter.

thesis.mechanism: Stable customer retention sustains the recurring-revenue base.

assessment.driver_statement: Stable customer retention sustains the recurring-revenue base.
assessment.rationale: The exact gross-retention measure directly supports a stable recurring-revenue base.

gold.rationale: The assessment is bound, directional, and limited to the retention mechanism.

cases.title: RPO growth needs a precise conversion follow-up

claim.normalized_statement: Remaining performance obligations increased 25% year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Contracted backlog converts into recognized revenue on schedule.

assessment.driver_statement: Contracted backlog converts into recognized revenue on schedule.
assessment.rationale: RPO growth is known, but the recognition schedule, cancellations, and renewal mix are absent.
assessment.follow_up_question: What share of current RPO is scheduled for recognition within twelve months, and did cancellations or renewal timing change?

gold.rationale: The assessment identifies the exact conversion gap and asks for evidence capable of closing it.

cases.title: Reported margin expansion directly supports scalable unit economics

claim.normalized_statement: Operating margin expanded by 350 basis points year over year.

thesis.mechanism: Operating-margin expansion demonstrates scalable unit economics.

assessment.driver_statement: Operating-margin expansion demonstrates scalable unit economics.
assessment.rationale: The claim directly reports the operating-margin expansion specified by the mechanism.

gold.rationale: The inference does not exceed the exact margin claim.

cases.title: Lower logo churn supports longer subscription lifetime

claim.normalized_statement: Monthly logo churn declined from 2.1% to 1.4%.

thesis.mechanism: Lower customer churn lengthens subscription lifetime.

assessment.driver_statement: Lower customer churn lengthens subscription lifetime.
assessment.rationale: The measured decline in logo churn is directionally consistent with longer customer lifetime.

gold.rationale: The assessment uses the exact churn metric without adding an unsupported financial conclusion.

cases.title: List-price growth needs realized-price and volume evidence

claim.normalized_statement: Published list prices increased by 8%.

thesis.mechanism: Price increases expand gross profit without damaging volume.

assessment.driver_statement: Price increases expand gross profit without damaging volume.
assessment.rationale: List prices are known, but realized net price, discounts, retained volume, and gross profit are not.
assessment.follow_up_question: How did realized net price, unit volume, customer retention, and gross margin change after the list-price increase?

gold.rationale: The follow-up covers both price realization and the volume condition in the mechanism.

cases.title: Signed contracts do not prove scheduled revenue conversion

claim.normalized_statement: The value of newly signed contracts increased 40% year over year.

assessment.driver_statement: Contracted backlog converts into revenue within twelve months.
assessment.rationale: Every newly signed contract will convert into revenue within twelve months without cancellation or delay.

cases.title: Insufficient label contradicts a rationale claiming direct proof

cases.title: Tax-rate follow-up cannot test price realization or volume retention
